name: ski
desc: Evade the deadly Yeti on your jet-powered skis
why: Eric Raymond's old terminal skiing game with a Yeti, a charming relic of classic Unix game culture.

brief.what_it_is: ski is a terminal game, written in Python per the man page, in which you ski down an endless slope while unable to see ahead, since your jet-powered skis are on backwards. The input is single-letter commands typed at a '?' prompt, one per turn (for example turn, jump, teleport, launch an ICBM, or summon the Fire Demon), and the output is an ASCII view of the slope drawn behind you. The goal is to avoid trees, ice, bare ground and the Yeti for as long as possible. The run ends when something bad happens, and the final score reflects distance skied, jumps, Yetis melted, and remaining health.
brief.why_it_exists: The author presents it as a silly, fun game that shows you do not need fancy graphical user interfaces to have a good time. It is a revival of a classic Unix-era game, originally by Mark Stevans for Roy's Games, Inc., with the Python implementation, colour support and the invisible shell monster added by Eric S. Raymond.
brief.how_it_works: The slope is shown as characters: '.' snow is safe, 'Y' trees hurt, ' ' bare ground can make you fall, '#' ice stops turning, and 'A' is the Yeti, which crawls toward you at one space per turn and grabs you within one space. Each turn you type a command letter (r, l, j, h, t, i, d, !, ?), and a number before a command repeats it, so the docs give "4l" as turn left four times. The Yeti melts when you steer clear of it on a sunny day, and another one appears later. The '!' command drops you into a Unix shell inside a space warp and returns you to the same spot afterward.

commands_seen.context: The SYNOPSIS line of the man page (ski(6)), the only invocation shown. Starts the game.

Example from the docs of a count prefix: 'Preceding any command with a number does that command repeatedly; thus, for example, "4l" is "turn left 4 times".' This is typed at the game's '?' prompt, not in the shell.
In-game key that displays command help (documented as a command, shown at the '?' prompt).
In-game key that spawns an invisible Unix shell; you can type shell commands and get returned to your slope afterward.

brief.install_notes: Installs with brew install ski, and the executable is named ski. The homepage says the code is usually packaged as 'ski' and offers a gzipped source tarball (ski-6.16.tar.gz). No accounts, hardware, or configuration are mentioned. Running it requires a terminal. Because it is a Python implementation according to the man page, a Python runtime may be needed if you go beyond the packaged build, but I did not see this stated explicitly in the README.
brief.standout: It is a deliberately absurd, text-only game that packs in nuclear ICBMs, hyperspace teleport, a Fire Demon, and a 'hide in a Unix shell' command, all rendered in ASCII. The skis-on-backwards premise makes the player steer by looking behind them, which is a clever twist on the usual skiing game.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists version 6.16 with a date of 05 Apr 2026 and a Recent Changes note about code-hardening changes. The man page was last updated 2026-02-01. The GitLab project was created April 26, 2019, and the homepage links to project news and a roadmap.
brief.caveats: Licensed under the BSD 2-Clause 'Simplified' License, according to the GitLab page. It is terminal-only, with no graphics. The homepage's Recent Changes line has an apparent typo, 'CharGPT 5.3', which I copied as written. The GitLab page I fetched did not show the README body, so I could not confirm the build or install steps beyond the homepage and man page. The homepage asks for support via Patreon and SubscribeStar.
quotes: A fun and very silly game that proves you don't need fancy graphical user interfaces to have a good time.
Steer clear from the Yeti, and he will melt after a while, since it is a sunny day.
